description: This course covers advanced topics in database systems, including distributed databases, NoSQL technologies such as MongoDB and Cassandra, and advanced SQL queries with window functions and common table expressions. It explores transaction management, concurrency control, and recovery mechanisms. The course also includes data warehousing, ETL processes, and OLAP operations. Students will study advanced indexing techniques, including B-trees, hash indexes, and spatial indexes. It delves into data mining techniques like association rule mining and clustering algorithms. The course also covers database security, including encryption, access control, and role-based permissions. Finally, it discusses database performance tuning, query optimization, and benchmarking standards such as TPC-C and TPC-H.

clos.text: Define the architecture and components of distributed database systems, including replication, partitioning, and fault tolerance.
Describe the query processing and optimization techniques used in modern relational and NoSQL databases.
Explain the principles of concurrency control, transaction management, and recovery in database systems.
Apply advanced indexing techniques and query optimization strategies to improve database performance.
Design and implement a secure and scalable database system using encryption, access control, and benchmarking standards.

topics: Data Warehousing Concepts and OLAP Operations
ETL Processes and Data Integration Techniques
Advanced Indexing Techniques: B-trees, Hash, and Spatial Indexes
Data Mining Techniques: Association Rule Mining and Clustering
Database Security: Encryption and Access Control
Performance Tuning and Benchmarking Standards (TPC-C, TPC-H)
Advanced Data Modeling and Normalization Techniques
Capstone Project: Integrating Advanced Database Concepts
